To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the developmental stage of each tooth in the jaw of Chalcides is accurately predicted from the developmental stage of its predecessor in the same position, or in the next position in the same jaw quadrant.

(i) the number of functional tooth positions in Chalcides is constant throughout life; (ii) replacement teeth are numerous whatever the age of the animal; (iii) the developmental stage of replacement teeth in a given position cannot be accurately predicted by the developmental stage of teeth in the opposite position; and (iv) the developmental stage in a given position can be accurately predicted by that of the replacement tooth that precedes it in the arcade.

(1) the number of tooth positions is constant in the dentary, maxilla, and premaxilla; (2) the developmental stage of each tooth is related to the stage of the preceding tooth; and (3) the developmental stage can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy.
